On The 5 th Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 59819 of 2025
 Aashish Agrawal
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Neeraj Soni, counsel for the applicant.
 Shri Romil Verma, G.A. for the State.
Perused the case diary / challan papers.

2. This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (439 of Cr.P.C.) as he/she is implicated in connection with Crime No.264/2021 registered at Police Station Kishanganj, District Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 406 and 120-B of IPC.
The applicant is in custody since 29/07/2022.
3. The allegation against the applicant is of his involvement in the aforesaid case of fraud to the tune of Rs.5 crore along with other accused persons Jitendra Verma, Sunil Sharma and Pramod.
4. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the co-accused Jitendra Verma has already been granted bail by the Supreme Court in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.1574/2023 dated 20/03/2023.

Counsel has submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:5944 2 MCRC-59819-2025 Jitendra Verma was the main conspirator and he has been granted bail by the Supreme Court only because he was lodged in jail since 20/07/2022, whereas the present applicant is also lodged in jail since 29/07/2022 and as of now only 5 witnesses have been examined out of 14 witnesses and there are no criminal antecedents of the applicant and the final conclusion of the trial Aashish Agrawal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99743608/
1 is likely to take sufficient long time, therefore, it is prayed that the application be allowed and the applicant be released on bail.
5. Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed the prayer, however, it is not disputed that no recovery has been made from the present applicant.
6. Having considered the rival submissions and perusal of the case diary, taking note of the fact that co-accused Jitendra Verma has already been granted bail by the Supreme Court on account of his period of incarceration which is also the fact of the present applicant and the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time, without reflecting anything on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is hereby allowed.
7. The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
